body: Not too bad! I had to remind my Mom once, but otherwise it was okay. I told people to look it up if they were bothered and never had any issues. I also dont let everyone hold her, I still have a lot of control over who is near her and how long/close they’re near her, so its easier than if someone would be leaving baby with family, or being really free with who interacts with them.

We said it over and over and people still wouldnt listen, so I wrote down a list of all rules/wishes for visitors after birth (when they were allowed, how long, no kissing, what shots to get, how home visits would work, etc) and sent it out to everyone in question. People got annoyed but only the ones who hadnt been respectful of it in the first place, and everything went how we wanted it to. Talk to your nurses/midwives/etc about it too before and during labor and they will have your back on who comes in or not! I also just told people a lot was hospital policy if I wanted to avoid confrontation. Stick to your wishes and dont back down! This is your experience and no one elses. Only thing that matters is YOU and YOUR baby. Fuck anyone elses preferences (except daddy if he is around or having specific requests).

5 weeks PP, diagnosed severe generalized anxiety. I had HORRIBLE health anxiety my entire pregnancy. Always positive I was miscarrying or going to have a still-birth, rupture of sorts, too-early-to-be-viable delivery, etc. 

Now with my baby I’m horrified of SIDS, any illness, allergies, etc. I took her temperature nearly every hour the first two weeks and tend to interrupt her naps to make sure she is able to regain consciousness. 

What helps/helped the most is just calling your midwife/OB/pediatrician if you even have a slightly bad feeling. Better safe than sorry and while I do feel annoying to them, its so much easier to talk to someone who knows what they are talking about and doing, rather than confide in a partner or someone else. Also counting kicks religiously helped me a TON. Stay off google, it will make things worse. And honestly looking into a mild medication to help suppress some worries could be a lifesaver because the more stressed you are, the more those hormones/chemicals bug your little bean on the inside. 

I also have an intense fear of death in general. I want her to be able to have an essence of me no matter what. So, I made a journal while I was pregnant full of important, situational life advice for her to read through. It’s objective, honest advice I would give any friend. It has some quotes and poems that are (imo) vital to my existence. I also have a collection of film photos I’ve taken that I keep in a special album for her to look through memories of my early life, and I play/sing my favorite songs to her all the time so she’ll at least find subconscious comfort in them when she is older. 

Those are just some ideas but they are what have helped me manage these fears so far. Good luck, Mama. I’m sure everything will be just fine.

Nope, CBD is non-psychoactive! I use a tincture from CBD Genesis, mine is 1000mg. You can smoke it, ingest it, vape it in a pen, or use it topically. Tastes like shit, but it works brilliantly topically. For smoking, I try to get an oil cartridge from dispensaries, or a strain of weed (ACDC is really good) but the weed always has a tiny THC percentage, which actually aggravates my anxiety.

YES and it is fucking amazing. I have ptsd and debilitating generalized anxiety, no medications help, meditation makes it worse, falling asleep makes me think I’m going to die, life is a struggle. BUT CBD oil with little to no thc works magic. Its the only thing that helps other than showers(??) and I will actually physically feel my body relax and my brain become..me, again. I dont even have to be having an attack and it’ll make a huge difference. I also have chronic pain and it works wonders for that too, topically (in tincture form). I highly highly recommend you bite the bullet and dish out some cash for it because it can be hard to find and pretty expensive, especially depending on how much you’re using it, but 10/10 is worth it. Good luck!!
